Tomato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease affecting tomato foliage, stems, and fruit. It creates dark concentric ring spots on mature leaves.
symptoms: Concentric brown spots on lower leaves
organic_treatment: Prune affected lower leaves immediately and dispose away from field
Apply copper octanoate or neem oil every 7-10 days
Mulch soil around base to prevent fungal spores splashing from soil
chemical_treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb fungicide at first sign of symptoms
Alternate with Azoxystrobin to prevent fungicide resistance
prevention: Maintain 24-36 inch spacing between plants for adequate airflow
Water exclusively at soil level using drip irrigation
Rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants for 3 seasons

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A devastating water mold that can rapidly destroy entire tomato fields during cool, damp weather.
symptoms: White fuzzy mold under leaf surfaces
organic_treatment: Remove and incinerate all infected plants immediately
Apply copper hydroxide spray preventive barrier
Ensure bio-pesticide Bacillus subtilis is applied to soil
chemical_treatment: Apply systemic fungicides containing Metalaxyl, Dimethomorph, or Cyazofamid
Spray at 5-7 day intervals during high risk weather
prevention: Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants nearby

Potato___Early_blight.description: Affects foliage and tubers, causing target spots on leaves and dark sunken lesions on potato tubers.
symptoms: Concentric dark brown circular leaf spots
Sunken dry rot spots on tubers
organic_treatment: Destroy infected vines 2 weeks before harvest
Apply copper sulfate or liquid kelp extract spray
chemical_treatment: Begin treatment when plants reach 8 inches in height
prevention: Ensure proper soil potassium and nitrogen fertility

Potato___Late_blight.description: Historically famous pathogen (causing the Irish Potato Famine) that rots foliage and tubers with extreme speed.
symptoms: White mold growth underneath leaf in humid morning
organic_treatment: Kill vines immediately if outbreak is detected to protect tubers
chemical_treatment: Apply systemic fungicides: Cymoxanil, Propamocarb, or Fluazinam
Spray every 5-7 days when weather is cool and rainy
prevention: Hill up soil well over potato tubers to prevent spore washed into soil
Destroy cull piles of leftover potatoes

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Wind-borne fungal spores produce reddish-brown powdery pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
symptoms: Powdery rust spores rubbing off on fingers
chemical_treatment: Apply Tebuconazole or Propiconazole triazole fungicides
Treat if rust affects >5% of leaves prior to silking
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids containing Rp genes
Plant early in the season to avoid peak spore flights

Apple___healthy.description: Apple tree leaf foliage is healthy, dark green, free of scab or rust spots.
organic_treatment: Apply balanced micronutrient foliar spray (zinc, boron)
prevention: Prune tree annually for open canopy structure

Tomato___healthy.description: Plant foliage is healthy, vibrant green with no visible signs of fungal lesions, bacterial spots, or viral chlorosis.
organic_treatment: Continue standard organic fertilization schedule (compost tea, balanced NPK)
prevention: Inspect foliage weekly for early warning signs
Maintain preventative bio-fungicide sprays during high humidity
